subproblem.title: Boundary estimate |∂T₁(fω)| ≤ (m+1)∫_{M₁}(|f||Dω| + |Df||ω|) dH^{m+1} for an integral current with unit-bounded orientation
subproblem.statement:
Setting: P, m ∈ ℕ; U, M₁ ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets; T₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U); ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1}. Assume:
(h2) T₁(θ) = ∫_{M₁} ξ(x)(θ(x)) dH^{m+1}(x) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), for μHE[m+1] restricted to M₁.
(h3) For μHE[m+1]⌞M₁-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every (m+1)-covector α, where ‖α‖ is the operator norm.
Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be differentiable, and let ω, F ∈ 𝒟^m(U) satisfy F(x) = f(x)·ω(x) for all x. Then, in [0, ∞],
ofReal |∂T₁(F)| ≤ ∫⁻_{M₁} ofReal((m+1)·(|f(x)|·‖Dω(x)‖ + ‖Df(x)‖·‖ω(x)‖)) dH^{m+1}(x),
with operator norms of Fréchet derivatives.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M₁ : Set (Euclid P)) (T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (m + 1)), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T₁ ω = ∫ x in M₁, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[m + 1].restrict M₁), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (m + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ ‖α‖) → ∀ (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (ω F : TestFormOn U m), Differentiable ℝ f → (∀ x, (F : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x = f x • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) → ENNReal.ofReal |T₁.boundary F| ≤ ∫⁻ x in M₁, ENNReal.ofReal (((m : ℝ) + 1) * (|f x| * ‖fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x‖ + ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ * ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x‖)) ∂μHE[m + 1]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: first half of step 5 of the parent proof. This is the parent's correction [D2] of the book's pointwise estimate |d(ζω) − ζ dω| ≤ c|ω| Σ_j σ_j^{n−1} on spt T₁ (proof of Simon 7.5.11, chapter-07.txt lines 1010–1013). Instead of a pointwise bound, |∂T₁(fω)| is bounded by the integral over M₁ of a pointwise bound for d(fω), using the unit bound (h3) on ξ.
Notation: dF(x) = Alt(DF(x)); in Mathlib, extDeriv F x = alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ F x). ν := μHE[m+1].restrict M₁.

1. (Integral form.) By definition of the boundary, ∂T₁(F) = T₁(dF), where dF ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) is the exterior derivative of F (exteriorDerivativeTestOn). By (h2), T₁(dF) = ∫ g dν, where g(x) := ξ(x)(dF(x)) ∈ ℝ.

2. (Integral bound without integrability.) For any measure ν and any real function g, ‖∫ g dν‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν (Mathlib enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). If g is not ν-integrable, the Bochner integral is 0 and the bound is trivial. For a real number r, ‖r‖ₑ = ofReal |r| (Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs). Hence ofReal |∂T₁(F)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal |g(x)| dν(x).

3. (Pointwise bound for dF.) Fix x ∈ ℝ^P.
   - ω is C^∞ (a test form), so it is differentiable at x; f is differentiable at x.
   - Since F = f·ω as functions, the product rule (Mathlib fderiv_smul) gives DF(x) = f(x)·Dω(x) + (Df(x)).smulRight(ω(x)), where (Df(x)).smulRight(ω(x)) is the map v ↦ Df(x)(v)·ω(x).
   - The triangle inequality gives ‖DF(x)‖ ≤ |f(x)|·‖Dω(x)‖ + ‖Df(x)‖·‖ω(x)‖. For the first term use ‖c·L‖ ≤ |c|·‖L‖ for the operator norm; in Lean this is ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le, because instance search does not find IsBoundedSMul ℝ (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) m) in this Mathlib snapshot. For the second term use ‖λ.smulRight v‖ = ‖λ‖·‖v‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply).
   - Alternation from (Euclid P →L Λ^m) to Λ^{m+1} increases the operator norm by at most the factor m + 1 (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_alternatizeUncurryFin_le).
   Therefore ‖dF(x)‖ ≤ (m + 1)·(|f(x)|·‖Dω(x)‖ + ‖Df(x)‖·‖ω(x)‖) =: h(x).

4. (Use of (h3).) For ν-a.e. x, (h3) applied with α := dF(x) gives |g(x)| = |ξ(x)(dF(x))| ≤ ‖dF(x)‖ ≤ h(x). Hence ofReal |g(x)| ≤ ofReal h(x) for ν-a.e. x. The lower Lebesgue integral is monotone under ν-a.e. inequalities, with no measurability needed (Mathlib lintegral_mono_ae). So ∫⁻ ofReal |g| dν ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal h dν.

5. (Conclusion.) Steps 2 and 4 give ofReal |∂T₁(F)| ≤ ∫⁻_{M₁} ofReal((m + 1)·(|f(x)|·‖Dω(x)‖ + ‖Df(x)‖·‖ω(x)‖)) dH^{m+1}(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: ofReal|∫ g dν| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|g| dν (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm; no integrability needed).
dF(x) = Alt(DF(x)) and DF(x) = f(x)Dω(x) + Df(x).smulRight(ω(x)), so ‖dF(x)‖ ≤ (m + 1)(|f(x)|‖Dω(x)‖ + ‖Df(x)‖‖ω(x)‖).
(h3) gives |ξ(x)(dF(x))| ≤ ‖dF(x)‖ for H^{m+1}⌞M₁-a.e. x; conclude with lintegral_mono_ae.

audit.reason: The exact ENNReal inequality matches the prose, including differentiability of f and the separate test-form hypothesis on F. The proof correctly combines the Fréchet product rule, operator-norm bounds, the m + 1 alternation factor, the simultaneous almost-everywhere covector bound, and unconditional Bochner/lower-integral domination. No integrability or measurability hypothesis is silently added.

subproblem.title: ∂T₁(η) = 0 when spt η meets closure(M₁) only inside M₁ (partition-of-unity localisation; Simon 7.5.11 (2), corrected)
subproblem.statement:
Setting: P, m ∈ ℕ; U, M₁ ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets (M₁ is not assumed measurable); T, T₁ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1)); ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1} (MultiVector P (m+1)). Assume:
(h1) ∂T = 0.
(h2) T₁(θ) = ∫_{M₁} ξ(x)(θ(x)) dH^{m+1}(x) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U). This is a Bochner integral for μHE[m+1] restricted to M₁.
(h4) Every z ∈ M₁ has an open set G ∋ z and a constant c ∈ ℝ with T₁(θ) = c·T(θ) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) with tsupport θ ⊆ G.
Then ∂T₁(η) = T₁(dη) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) (TestFormOn U m) with closure(M₁) ∩ tsupport η ⊆ M₁.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M₁ : Set (Euclid P)) (T T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (m + 1)), T.boundary = 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T₁ ω = ∫ x in M₁, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]) → (∀ z ∈ M₁, ∃ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G ∧ z ∈ G ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) ⊆ G → T₁ ω = c * T ω) → ∀ η : TestFormOn U m, closure M₁ ∩ tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ M₁ → T₁.boundary η = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof. This is identity (2) in the proof of Simon 7.5.11 (chapter-07.txt lines 996–999): 'if ζ ≡ 0 in some neighborhood of spt T ∖ M₁, then T₁(d(ζω)) = T(d(ζω)) = ∂T(ζω) = 0'. It is made rigorous by the parent's correction [D3]: M₁ is separated from the rest of spt T by a partition of unity subordinate to the neighbourhoods G of (h4), on which T₁ is a multiple of T.
Notation: for a form F, dF(x) is the alternation of DF(x). The operator d is linear on test forms and does not enlarge topological supports (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). By definition ∂S(η) = S(dη). In Lean, `open scoped Manifold` is needed for 𝓘(ℝ, Euclid P); do not open the ContDiff scope, because it makes ω a token.

Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) satisfy closure(M₁) ∩ tsupport η ⊆ M₁.

1. (Compactness.) Put K₁ := closure(M₁) ∩ tsupport η. It is a closed subset of the compact set tsupport η (η has compact support), hence compact. By hypothesis K₁ ⊆ M₁.

2. (Finite cover.) For each z ∈ K₁ ⊆ M₁, (h4) gives an open set G_z ∋ z and c_z ∈ ℝ with T₁(θ) = c_z·T(θ) for all θ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) with tsupport θ ⊆ G_z. The sets G_z, z ∈ K₁, form an open cover of the compact set K₁. Choose z_1, …, z_L ∈ K₁ (L ≥ 0 is allowed) with K₁ ⊆ W := G_{z_1} ∪ … ∪ G_{z_L}. W is open.

3. (Partition of unity.) ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, so there is an open set O₁ with K₁ ⊆ O₁ and closure(O₁) ⊆ W (Mathlib exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure).
   - closure(O₁) is closed and covered by the open sets G_{z_l}.
   - Apply Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate to ℝ^P as a manifold modelled on itself with 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P); it is Hausdorff, σ-compact and finite-dimensional.
   - This gives a smooth partition of unity (ψ_l)_{l=1..L} on closure(O₁) subordinate to (G_{z_l}). Each ψ_l : ℝ^P → ℝ is C^∞ (contMDiff_iff_contDiff), tsupport ψ_l ⊆ G_{z_l}, and Σ_l ψ_l(x) = 1 for every x ∈ closure(O₁).
   Let χ := Σ_l ψ_l. It is C^∞ and χ = 1 on O₁. If L = 0, then χ ≡ 0 and O₁ = ∅.

4. (Decomposition.) Put η₀(x) := (1 − χ(x))·η(x) and η_l(x) := ψ_l(x)·η(x) for l = 1, …, L.
   - Each is a C^∞ form, as the product of a C^∞ function with the C^∞ form η.
   - Its support is contained in support η. So it has compact support and topological support ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ U. Hence η₀, η_l ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
   - Pointwise, η₀ + Σ_l η_l = (1 − χ + Σ_l ψ_l)·η = η. So η = η₀ + Σ_l η_l in 𝒟^m(U).
   - Since ∂T₁ is linear, ∂T₁(η) = ∂T₁(η₀) + Σ_l ∂T₁(η_l).

5. (∂T₁(η₀) = 0.) Let V := O₁ ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ tsupport η), an open set.
   - η₀ vanishes on V: on O₁ we have χ = 1, and off tsupport η we have η = 0.
   - M₁ ⊆ V: if x ∈ M₁ and x ∈ tsupport η, then x ∈ closure(M₁) ∩ tsupport η = K₁ ⊆ O₁.
   Now let x ∈ M₁. η₀ is identically 0 on the neighbourhood V of x, so x ∉ tsupport η₀. Hence x ∉ tsupport dη₀ and dη₀(x) = 0.
   By (h2), ∂T₁(η₀) = T₁(dη₀) = ∫_{M₁} ξ(x)(dη₀(x)) dH^{m+1}(x). At every x ∈ M₁ the integrand is ξ(x)(0) = 0, because ξ(x) is linear. So the integral is 0 by Mathlib setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero, which needs no measurability of M₁.

6. (∂T₁(η_l) = 0.) dη_l ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), and tsupport dη_l ⊆ tsupport η_l ⊆ tsupport ψ_l ⊆ G_{z_l}; here support(ψ_l·η) ⊆ support ψ_l (Mathlib tsupport_smul_subset_left). Since z_l ∈ M₁, (h4) and (h1) give
   ∂T₁(η_l) = T₁(dη_l) = c_{z_l}·T(dη_l) = c_{z_l}·∂T(η_l) = c_{z_l}·0 = 0.

7. By steps 4–6, ∂T₁(η) = 0 + Σ_l 0 = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: K₁ := closure(M₁) ∩ tsupport η is compact and contained in M₁; cover it by finitely many (h4) neighbourhoods G_{z_l}.
Choose an open O₁ ⊇ K₁ with closure(O₁) ⊆ ⋃_l G_{z_l}, and a smooth partition of unity (ψ_l) on closure(O₁) subordinate to (G_{z_l}). Then χ := Σ_l ψ_l = 1 on O₁.
η = (1 − χ)η + Σ_l ψ_l η in 𝒟^m(U), and ∂T₁ is linear.
(1 − χ)η vanishes on the open set O₁ ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ tsupport η) ⊇ M₁. So d((1 − χ)η) = 0 at every point of M₁, and ∂T₁((1 − χ)η) = 0 by (h2) and setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero.
tsupport d(ψ_l η) ⊆ G_{z_l}, so ∂T₁(ψ_l η) = c_{z_l}·∂T(ψ_l η) = 0 by (h4) and (h1).

audit.reason: The prose and type agree, including arbitrary U and potentially nonmeasurable M₁. Compactness, finite localization, and the subordinate smooth partition justify the decomposition. The remainder vanishes near every point of M₁; the other terms vanish by local proportionality and ∂T = 0. The cited set-integral result requires no measurability of M₁. Empty covers and support conditions are handled without circularity.

subproblem.title: Finite ball cover of a compact Hausdorff-null set with small Σσ_j^m (covering step of Simon 7.5.11)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let Z ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)) be compact with μH[m](Z) = 0, where μH[m] is Mathlib's m-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Then for all real ε > 0 and δ > 0 there exist J ∈ ℕ, points p_1, …, p_J ∈ Z and radii σ_1, …, σ_J ∈ ℝ such that 0 < σ_j < δ for every j, Z ⊆ B(p_1, σ_1) ∪ … ∪ B(p_J, σ_J) (open balls), and Σ_{j=1}^J σ_j^m < ε.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Z : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact Z → μH[(m : ℝ)] Z = 0 → ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∃ (J : ℕ) (p : Fin J → Euclid P) (σ : Fin J → ℝ), (∀ j, p j ∈ Z) ∧ (∀ j, 0 < σ j ∧ σ j < δ) ∧ Z ⊆ ⋃ j, ball (p j) (σ j) ∧ ∑ j, σ j ^ m < ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof. This is the covering in the proof of Simon 7.5.11 (chapter-07.txt lines 1001–1004): 'since H^{n−1}(sing T) = 0 (by 5.8) and since sing T ∩ spt ω is compact, we can find a finite collection of balls B_{σ_j}(ξ_j), j = 1, …, P, with ξ_j ∈ sing T ∩ spt ω and Σ σ_j^{n−1} < ε'. Two changes from the printed text:
- the radius bound σ_j < δ is added, because the parent needs 2σ_j below the density radius and σ_j ≤ 1;
- m here plays the role of n − 1.
Notation: μH[m] is Mathlib's Hausdorff measure, which has the same null sets as Simon's H^m. ediam is the extended diameter. B(p, σ) is the open ball.

1. (Case m = 0.) Suppose x ∈ Z. By Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton, μH[0]({x}) = 1. Since {x} ⊆ Z, monotonicity gives 1 ≤ μH[0](Z) = 0, a contradiction. Hence Z = ∅.
   Take J = 0, the empty families. The conditions on the p_j and σ_j are vacuous, Z = ∅ is contained in the empty union, and the empty sum is 0 < ε.

2. (Case m ≥ 1: constants.) Put η := ε/2^{m+2} > 0 and δ' := min(δ/2, 1, η) > 0. Then δ' ≤ δ/2, δ' ≤ 1 and δ' ≤ η.

3. (Countable cover.) By Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_apply,
   μH[m](Z) = ⨆_{r>0} ⨅ { Σ'_{n∈ℕ} ⨆_{t_n ≠ ∅} ediam(t_n)^m : Z ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, ediam(t_n) ≤ r for all n }.
   Take r := δ/2 > 0 as an extended real. The infimum for this r is at most μH[m](Z) = 0 < η. Hence there is a sequence of sets (t_n)_{n∈ℕ} with:
   - Z ⊆ ⋃_n t_n;
   - ediam(t_n) ≤ δ/2 for all n;
   - S_∞ := Σ'_n [t_n ≠ ∅] ediam(t_n)^m < η.
   Each ediam(t_n) is finite. Let d_n ∈ [0, δ/2] denote its real value.

4. (Centres and radii.) Let I := {n ∈ ℕ : t_n ∩ Z ≠ ∅}. For n ∈ I choose p_n ∈ t_n ∩ Z. For every n put τ_n := δ'·2^{−(n+1)} and σ_n := d_n + τ_n. Then:
   (a) 0 < τ_n ≤ δ'/2 ≤ δ/4. Hence 0 < σ_n ≤ δ/2 + δ/4 < δ.
   (b) For n ∈ I, t_n ⊆ B(p_n, σ_n). Indeed, if z ∈ t_n then z and p_n both lie in t_n, so dist(z, p_n) ≤ ediam(t_n) = d_n < σ_n.
   (c) Z ⊆ ⋃_{n∈I} B(p_n, σ_n). Indeed, each z ∈ Z lies in some t_n. Then z ∈ t_n ∩ Z, so n ∈ I, and z ∈ B(p_n, σ_n) by (b).
   (d) σ_n^m ≤ 2^m (d_n^m + η·2^{−(n+1)}). Indeed:
       - σ_n ≤ 2·max(d_n, τ_n), and t ↦ t^m is monotone on [0, ∞);
       - so σ_n^m ≤ 2^m·max(d_n, τ_n)^m = 2^m·max(d_n^m, τ_n^m) ≤ 2^m (d_n^m + τ_n^m);
       - finally τ_n^m ≤ τ_n ≤ η·2^{−(n+1)}, because 0 ≤ τ_n ≤ 1, m ≥ 1 and δ' ≤ η.

5. (Finite subcover and the sum.) Z is compact and covered by the open balls B(p_n, σ_n), n ∈ I. Choose a finite set S ⊆ I with Z ⊆ ⋃_{n∈S} B(p_n, σ_n).
   - First sum. For n ∈ S the set t_n is nonempty, so the n-th term of the series S_∞ is ediam(t_n)^m = d_n^m (as extended reals). A finite partial sum of a series of nonnegative terms is at most its sum (Mathlib ENNReal.sum_le_tsum, after embedding S into ℕ). Hence Σ_{n∈S} d_n^m ≤ S_∞ < η.
   - Second sum. Σ_{n∈S} 2^{−(n+1)} ≤ Σ_{n≥0} 2^{−(n+1)} = 1.
   - Conclusion. By 4(d), Σ_{n∈S} σ_n^m ≤ 2^m (Σ_{n∈S} d_n^m + η·Σ_{n∈S} 2^{−(n+1)}) < 2^m (η + η) = 2^{m+1}·ε/2^{m+2} = ε/2 < ε.

6. (Re-indexing.) Enumerate S as n_1, …, n_J with J := |S| (e.g. via Finset.equivFin), and put p_j := p_{n_j}, σ_j := σ_{n_j}. Then:
   - p_j ∈ Z, because n_j ∈ I;
   - 0 < σ_j < δ by 4(a);
   - Z ⊆ ⋃_j B(p_j, σ_j) by step 5;
   - Σ_j σ_j^m = Σ_{n∈S} σ_n^m < ε.
   ∎
proof_key_steps: m = 0: μH[0]({x}) = 1 forces Z = ∅, so the empty family (J = 0) works.
m ≥ 1: from hausdorffMeasure_apply and μH[m](Z) = 0, get a countable cover (t_n) with ediam(t_n) ≤ δ/2 and Σ'_n [t_n ≠ ∅] ediam(t_n)^m < η := ε/2^{m+2}.
For n with t_n ∩ Z ≠ ∅, pick p_n ∈ t_n ∩ Z and σ_n := d_n + δ'·2^{−(n+1)}, where δ' = min(δ/2, 1, η). Then 0 < σ_n < δ, t_n ⊆ B(p_n, σ_n) and σ_n^m ≤ 2^m (d_n^m + η·2^{−(n+1)}).
By compactness, choose a finite subcover S. Then Σ_{n∈S} σ_n^m < 2^{m+1}·η = ε/2.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly includes compactness, Hausdorff nullity, positive ε and δ, centres in Z, strict radius bounds, coverage, and the small sum. The proof correctly handles m = 0, extracts a countable cover, enlarges diameters by positive summable radii, bounds the finite subcover sum, and reindexes by Fin J. It is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Smooth cut-off ζ = ∏(1 − φ_j) vanishing on finitely many balls, with a gradient bound (Simon 7.5.11, corrected)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ), ∃ c₀ : ℝ, 0 ≤ c₀ ∧ ∀ (J : ℕ) (p : Fin J → Euclid P) (σ : Fin J → ℝ), (∀ j, 0 < σ j) → ∃ ζ : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ζ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ζ x ∧ ζ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ j, ∀ x ∈ ball (p j) (σ j), ζ x = 0) ∧ (∀ x, 1 - ζ x ≤ ∑ j, (ball (p j) (2 * σ j)).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x) ∧ ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ ≤ ∑ j, (ball (p j) (2 * σ j)).indicator (fun _ => c₀ / σ j) x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 3 of the parent proof. This is Simon's cut-off in the proof of 7.5.11 (chapter-07.txt lines 1004–1009): 'let φ_j ∈ C_c^∞ be such that φ_j ≡ 1 on B_{σ_j}(ξ_j), φ_j = 0 on ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ B_{2σ_j}(ξ_j), and 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1. Now choose ζ = ∏ φ_j …'. Two departures:
- Correction [D1]: the cut-off must vanish near the singular points, so ζ := ∏_j (1 − φ_j). The book prints ζ = ∏ φ_j.
- The printed gradient bound |Dζ| ≤ Σ_j |Dφ_j| ≤ Σ_j c/σ_j is recorded with the indicator of B(p_j, 2σ_j), which the parent's integrated estimate [D2] needs.

1. (Model bump and c₀.) Fix P. Let φ₀ : ℝ^P → ℝ be the smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius 1 and outer radius 3/2 (Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = 1, rOut = 3/2). Then:
   - φ₀ is C^∞ and 0 ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1;
   - φ₀(y) = 1 for ‖y‖ ≤ 1 (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall);
   - the support of φ₀ is the open ball B(0, 3/2) (ContDiffBump.support_eq), so φ₀(y) = 0 for ‖y‖ ≥ 3/2.
   φ₀ is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz (Mathlib ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport). Let c₀ ≥ 0 be a Lipschitz constant of φ₀; one may take c₀ = sup‖Dφ₀‖. Then c₀ depends only on P.

2. (Rescaled bumps.) Let J, the points p_j and the radii σ_j > 0 be given. Put φ_j(x) := φ₀(σ_j^{−1}(x − p_j)).
   (a) φ_j is C^∞, being φ₀ composed with an affine map, and 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1.
   (b) If x ∈ B(p_j, σ_j), then ‖σ_j^{−1}(x − p_j)‖ = dist(x, p_j)/σ_j < 1, so φ_j(x) = 1.
   (c) If dist(y, p_j) > (3/2)σ_j, then ‖σ_j^{−1}(y − p_j)‖ > 3/2, so φ_j(y) = 0. Now let x ∉ B(p_j, 2σ_j), i.e. dist(x, p_j) ≥ 2σ_j > (3/2)σ_j. Then φ_j vanishes identically on the open neighbourhood {y : dist(y, p_j) > (3/2)σ_j} of x, so φ_j(x) = 0 and Dφ_j(x) = 0.
   (d) The map x ↦ σ_j^{−1}(x − p_j) is σ_j^{−1}-Lipschitz, so φ_j is (c₀/σ_j)-Lipschitz. The derivative of a K-Lipschitz function has operator norm at most K (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Hence ‖Dφ_j(x)‖ ≤ c₀/σ_j for all x. This is the argument of SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_whitneyBump_derivative_bound.
   Combining (a)–(d), for every x:
   - φ_j(x) ≤ 1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}(x);
   - ‖Dφ_j(x)‖ ≤ (c₀/σ_j)·1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}(x).

3. (Definition of ζ.) Put ζ(x) := ∏_{j=1}^J (1 − φ_j(x)); if J = 0 this is the empty product, ζ ≡ 1.
   - ζ is C^∞ as a finite product of C^∞ functions.
   - Each factor lies in [0, 1], so 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1.
   - If x ∈ B(p_j, σ_j) for some j, the j-th factor is 1 − 1 = 0 by 2(b), so ζ(x) = 0.

4. (Bound for 1 − ζ.) Claim: for any finite family a_i ∈ [0, 1], 1 − ∏_i (1 − a_i) ≤ Σ_i a_i. Proof by induction over the finite index set:
   - For the empty family both sides are 0.
   - Adding an index k: put Π := ∏_i (1 − a_i) ∈ [0, 1] over the old indices. Then 1 − (1 − a_k)Π = (1 − Π) + a_k·Π ≤ Σ_i a_i + a_k.
   Apply the claim with a_j = φ_j(x) and then use step 2: 1 − ζ(x) ≤ Σ_j φ_j(x) ≤ Σ_j 1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}(x).

5. (Gradient bound.) Each 1 − φ_j is differentiable with derivative −Dφ_j(x). By the product rule for finite products (Mathlib HasFDerivAt.finsetProd),
   Dζ(x) = Σ_j (∏_{i≠j} (1 − φ_i(x)))·(−Dφ_j(x)).
   Each product ∏_{i≠j} (1 − φ_i(x)) lies in [0, 1]. The triangle inequality and ‖c·L‖ ≤ |c|·‖L‖ then give
   ‖Dζ(x)‖ ≤ Σ_j ‖Dφ_j(x)‖ ≤ Σ_j (c₀/σ_j)·1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}(x),
   using step 2. In Lean, use ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le for ‖c·L‖ ≤ |c|·‖L‖. Since ζ is differentiable, fderiv ℝ ζ x = Dζ(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix the ContDiffBump φ₀ (rIn = 1, rOut = 3/2) and a Lipschitz constant c₀ ≥ 0 of φ₀; c₀ depends only on P.

φ_j(x) = φ₀(σ_j^{−1}(x − p_j)) is C^∞ with values in [0, 1], equals 1 on B(p_j, σ_j), vanishes near every x ∉ B(p_j, 2σ_j) and is (c₀/σ_j)-Lipschitz. Hence φ_j ≤ 1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)} and ‖Dφ_j‖ ≤ (c₀/σ_j)·1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}.
ζ := ∏_j (1 − φ_j) is C^∞, takes values in [0, 1] and vanishes on each B(p_j, σ_j).
By induction, 1 − ∏(1 − a_j) ≤ Σ a_j for a_j ∈ [0, 1]; hence 1 − ζ ≤ Σ_j 1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}.
The product rule with 0 ≤ ∏_{i≠j}(1 − φ_i) ≤ 1 gives ‖Dζ‖ ≤ Σ_j ‖Dφ_j‖ ≤ Σ_j (c₀/σ_j)·1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}.
